rationale: C02 is a direct and material drafting template: both orders establish geographically bounded airspace reservations through numbered boundary descriptions and then use nearly identical language imposing the same Civil Aeronautics Act penalties for unauthorized aircraft navigation. C15 also shares the airspace-reservation machinery and penalty clause but adds a substantially more elaborate regulatory regime. C12 merely refers to airspace reservations as one category of protected installations and is therefore a distant third.

shared_material.child_excerpt: All that area within the City of Washington, D.C., lying within the following-described boundaries: Beginning at ... thence ... the point of beginning.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: All that area within the United States lying within each of the following-described boundaries: 1. Clinton Engineering Works ... Beginning at ... thence ... the point of beginning.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same operative structure: establish an airspace reservation by specifying one or more numbered areas through coordinate or landmark-based perimeter descriptions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any person navigating an aircraft within this airspace reservation in violation of the provisions of this order will be subject to the penalties prescribed in the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938 (52 Stat. 973), as amended.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any person navigating an aircraft within any of these airspace reservations in violation of the provisions of this order will be subject to the penalties prescribed in the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938 (52 Stat. 973), as amended.
shared_material.explanation: The enforcement sentence is virtually verbatim, differing only to accommodate one reservation rather than several.
